title: Method Lanes

scenario.intro: Four actions share the {{thing}} desk, but every one of them is waiting in the GET lane. Requests for the other three bounce with 405 Method Not Allowed.
scenario.goal: Put each action on the HTTP method that means it: reading a {{thing}}, sending a new one, changing part of one, and cancelling one.

objective: Every request finds its action because it used the right method.
rules: Changing a {{thing}}'s address updates only part of it.
starter_code:
from fastapi import FastAPI, Response

app = FastAPI()

# The HTTP method each action listens on
# >>> EDIT START
READ = "GET"
SEND = "GET"
CHANGE = "GET"
CANCEL = "GET"
# <<< EDIT END


async def read(item_id: int) -> dict[str, object]:
    return {"action": "read", "id": item_id}


async def send() -> dict[str, object]:
    return {"action": "send"}


async def change(item_id: int) -> dict[str, object]:
    return {"action": "change", "id": item_id}


async def cancel(item_id: int) -> Response:
    return Response(status_code=204)


app.add_api_route("/{{thing}}s/{item_id}", read, methods=[READ])
app.add_api_route("/{{thing}}s", send, methods=[SEND], status_code=201)
app.add_api_route("/{{thing}}s/{item_id}", change, methods=[CHANGE])
app.add_api_route("/{{thing}}s/{item_id}", cancel, methods=[CANCEL])

hints.text: Same path, different method, different meaning. Which method creates something new?
Changing only part of a {{thing}} is not PUT (that replaces all of it).
Something like: SEND = "POST", and removing a {{thing}} has a method named exactly after it.

dialogue.start: Everyone is stuck in the GET lane. Sort them out!
dialogue.success: Every lane flows. Methods say what to do, and the tower listens.
dialogue.fail: Some requests still hit a closed lane (405). Check which action they wanted.
